precepts.why: This is what you men don’t want to be. When we started off it was three families, boots on the ground; we didn’t drag people from old congregations with us. You’re not a teacher of God if you have to steal, trick or beguile people to follow you. “Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them”: if you have to draw away disciples after you, you are not of the elect; you are a deceiver, a traitor, a defector, a derelict, treacherous.

precepts.why:
Sopater of Berea was the first name, so here is Berea. “And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.” Paul went into a synagogue of the Jews. “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica,” The Jews that were in Berea were more noble than the Jews in Thessalonica. How so? “in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” They received what Paul was teaching with all readiness of mind, but they continued searching the scriptures daily whether such things were so.

“Therefore many of them believed;” Many of them, and guess who one of them was: Sopater, the name we just read from Berea, was one of them which believed. “also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
Now Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica. “Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,” Three sabbath days Paul reasoned with them out of the scriptures. “Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ. And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.”

So out of Thessalonica, notice these people that believed: two of the names we just read, Aristarchus and Secundus, helped Paul set up the seven churches of Asia Minor. What always catches the eye is that you had chief women in the church; that is Titus 2, those are the chief women. And it talks about the Greeks, which we deal with a little later on.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus: the semicolon shows that Gaius and Timotheus were of Derbe. “Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.” To Derbe. “And when they had preached the gospel to that city,” When they preached the gospel to that city, Derbe, “and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,” So you have believers that came out of Derbe, such as Gaius.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Timotheus was mentioned with Derbe. “Then came he to Derbe and Lystra:” Here we go, Derbe again. “and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:” So the mother followed the laws of Moses, and then she believed, accepted Christ; but his father was a Greek. That is always the stipulation, and the Greeks are dealt with in 2 Maccabees.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: Of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus: you have people that came out of Asia that believed. “And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.” Jews and Greeks. When you read the term Greeks, most Christians will say, see, it is for all nations. But 2 Maccabees 4 shows what the Bible says about the Greeks.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
This explains the term Greeks, and yes, Maccabees is canon. “But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,” Jason was a wicked Israelite who laboured underhand to become high priest. That wasn't his office, but he laboured underhandedly to become high priest. “Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:” He was paying for this office, big money. “Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.” He wanted the Israelite men that practised these trainings to be called Antiochians. “Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.” He brought the Israelites to the Greekish fashion. This is why the Protestants didn't want us to understand this: you had wicked men who made a covenant with the Greeks to bring the Israelites to the Greekish fashion.

“Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;” Jason was a wicked Israelite. “That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple,” They despised the temple of God, “and neglecting the sacrifices,” neglected the sacrifices, “hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;” This was the origin of the Olympics. “Not setting by the honours of their fathers,” Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses and so forth; they didn't set by them. “but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.” The Israelites liked the glory of the Greeks best of all.

“By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly,” Notice the wording, so earnestly. We dressed Greek, we spoke Greek, we ate Greek, we started to worship the Greek gods. That is what the Israelites started to do. “and unto whom they desired to be like in all things.” Our forefathers desired to be like the Greeks in all things.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
While Jason was striving underhanded to force Israel to become Greeks, laws were being set up by Antiochus the king. “Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” It was against Greek law to call ourselves a Jew. This is the history the Christians are unaware of. TD Jakes is unaware of this, Creflo is unaware of this, and if they do know it and don't teach it they are wicked as hell, because they have everybody thinking that when you go to Galatians 3:28, there is no difference between Jew or Greek, so everybody is in. No: it is telling you they made laws that we couldn't call ourselves Jews.

“And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices;” They forced us to celebrate birthdays, the king's birth. That was never the Israelite custom; that was never God's law, to celebrate birthdays. When you read about birthdays in the Bible some calamity always happened: Herod's birthday, and John was beheaded; Pharaoh's birthday. It was always some death, so honouring your day was always against God's law. So now here you are today, mostly you women: it's my son's birthday, can we celebrate the birthday? No, because death always followed behind that. We were forced to do that filth, that evil. “and when the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.” You see that word compelled? They forced us to celebrate the king's birthday. We are not supposed to be celebrating nobody's birthdays; get it through your heads.

“Moreover there went out a decree to the neighbour cities of the heathen, by the suggestion of Ptolemee, against the Jews, that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices:” Ptolemee the Greek said we must observe the same fashions as the Greeks and be partakers of their sacrifices: when they sacrifice to Bacchus we are supposed to sacrifice to Bacchus, to Zeus, to Mercury, and so forth. “And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death.” The Gentiles there is making reference to the Greeks. Christians need to understand this: there were laws in place forbidding us to call ourselves Jews, forbidding us to call ourselves Israelites, and if we did not conform to become Greeks we were put to death. “Then might a man have seen the present misery.” Many of our ancestors saw present misery.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why: This is what they do. “There is neither Jew nor Greek,” They say, see, everybody is in. Listen: there is neither Jew nor Greek, why? Because they are one race of people. The Greeks Paul went to were the Jews who were forbidden to call themselves Jews and were forced to eat Greek, speak Greek, dress Greek, worship Greek. Paul had to undo all that madness that our people were in. “there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.” So what is Paul talking about? Unity. He is unifying the nation of Israel once again at that time. It is the same mission that we are on today, the same mission.

points: Testifying both to the Jews and also to the Greeks: testifying both to the southern kingdom and northern kingdom.

In Liberia, on the way to a radio show, we saw a young girl, maybe 10 or 11, washing clothes by hand in a pot on a Sunday: washing her little brother's uniform to prepare for school on Monday. When we came out, she was giving her kid brothers a bath in a bucket. Some of you walk into a store and buy deodorant; some of our brothers and sisters have to choose between deodorant and food. I am not saying that to degrade our brothers and sisters on the continent; I'm showing you that you should wake up every day and thank the Lord for where you're at. And some of you cannot even do that. What do you do? Complain, complain, complain. God hates a complainer. You complain about everything; you come here, you're still complaining.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there. Brothers, understand something: when you leave your house, you're traveling. Paul was saying he's going to Jerusalem and he doesn't know what's going to happen; they might kill him. Once you say, I want to travel international with you brothers, and you got a good report, understand there's a chance you might not come back. Always keep that in your head, because the minute you forget that, you're going to let your guard down. When you always remember it, that keeps you sharp. Same way you go to camp every Sabbath: there's a chance you might not come back. Keep that same mindset.

We were in Liberia. Some of you don't know the history: Liberia has been through two civil wars, horrible civil wars. Some of the young men in our camp right now, 24, 25, 26 years old, went through the civil war as kids. They saw some horrible things. How many of you have ever seen civil war? None of you. So how dare you complain? You got some nerve complaining. You have no idea the blessing you have, that the Most High let you grow up in this country.

points: But none of these things move me. Paul was saying death did not move me. I'm not afraid of death, I'm not afraid of affliction, I'm not afraid of getting locked up. Paul was ready to sacrifice for this truth, because Paul understood what he was called for, and what comes with that position.

points: Disciple means student. Paul went into Macedonia and Greece, and there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timotheus, and of Asia Tychicus and Trophimus.

“For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock”: that's what he is, he is a grievous wolf. You ever see a wolf when it's attacking? A pack of wolves won't let the animal go; the animal will be trying to run away limping and everything, they'll follow it. That's why they call them grievous wolves, they cause grief.

“Not sparing the flock”: they don't care about the congregation. His agenda is not to teach you, it's to reach you so he could use you as merchandise and make money off of you. “Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

points: Revelation 3 is part two of the message to the seven churches, and it opens with a little history regarding the seven churches out of the book of Acts. If you have never read the book of Acts you are not going to understand the epistles of Paul, and you are not going to understand the opening chapters of Revelation either. This is the establishing of the seven churches of Asia Minor: Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea, Smyrna and Ephesus, the green area on the map. We are going to find out who established them.

“And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia. And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece, And there abode three months.” You see that: he and they abode three months. Captains, we have to get on this level. We might not be able to stay a year, two years, three, Lord's will in the future, but at least three months. We stayed one month in Sierra Leone, and the brothers and sisters that helped us do that are definitely going to get their blessing when the Lord returns, and he may be giving you blessings right now.
“And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

points: “And there accompanied him into Asia” This is what we want: there accompanied him into Asia, that green area, Asia or Asia Minor. “Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.” Those names mentioned that went with Paul to Asia Minor are the names of the men that helped Paul set up Asia Minor. Sopater was one of the Bereans that believed (Acts 17:10-12). Aristarchus and Secundus were of the believers out of Thessalonica (Acts 17:1-4). Gaius and Timotheus were of Derbe, where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel (Acts 14:20-21; Acts 16:1). Tychicus and Trophimus were of Asia, where all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks (Acts 19:10).

When you read the term Greeks, most Christians will say, see, it is for all nations. But the Bible shows who the Greeks were: 2 Maccabees 4 and 6 show wicked men like Jason who made a covenant with the Greeks to bring the Israelites to the Greekish fashion, and laws under which it was not lawful to keep sabbath days or to profess yourself at all to be a Jew, and whoso would not conform to the manners of the Gentiles was put to death. That is the history the Christians are unaware of. And the white scholars know who those Greeks were. The Encyclopedia of the Jewish Diaspora, Origins, Experiences and Culture, volume one, edited by Avrum Ehrlich, one of the books they use in the top theology schools, says that in spite of attempts to show that the Jews in the western diaspora knew Hebrew, it is common knowledge that basically they knew only Greek; the Jews of the West knew neither Hebrew nor Aramaic, and their religious lives, including the reading of the Torah and prayer, were conducted solely in Greek. The Torah was translated into Greek in the third century BCE. In certain rabbinic circles the translation into Greek was viewed as a necessity of the times: the sages recognized that there were entire diaspora communities that spoke only Greek, and that these would be lost to the Jewish people in the absence of an authentic translation. That is why a lot of communities of the Israelites only spoke Greek; they were forced into that. And rabbinic literature almost totally ignores the vast western diaspora that existed at the time, which is particularly noticeable compared with the relatively large number of places in this diaspora mentioned in chapter 2 of Acts, in the chapters describing the journeys of Paul, and in the Pauline epistles, which give a comprehensive picture of the geography of the western Jewish Greek-speaking diaspora in the first century. So the scholars know that Paul was not going to all nations; Paul was going to the Greek-speaking Jews. This is the history our people don't know. You sit in church and be a dummy, a donkey, the Donkey of the Day, not knowing what this history is talking about.

So the seven churches were all following the teachings of the twelve apostles. They were set up by Paul and those men, Sopater of Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica, Gaius and Timothy of Derbe, Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia, and Barnabas also; those were the key figures that set up the seven churches of Asia Minor, all under the twelve apostles. Did some of them start going off? Yes, some of them started going the hell off, just like today: across the various IUIC camps you see which schools are weaker than others, which are more advanced in teaching and understanding, which have more zeal and which don't. Likewise here. This is why Christ said to John, send these letters unto the seven churches of Asia.
